name: operating
words: the Operating State — the five measurements (Trust · Recall · Efficiency · Experience · Cost), the kernel's watches and intention on them, thumbs, summon, the critic's proposals, a repo'd graph inside the hull
text: THE OPERATING STATE (Phase 8 sp5, canon 0010 §7) is the kernel's top-level scorecard — JB's five Kernel Strategic Measurements, each 1.0 at the ideal, read live off the ground and watched like any metric. At v0 they are coverage ratios, named v0 and refined when their richer sources land: TRUST = the graded live replies that passed (A · B · C) over all graded replies — the grader's signed verdicts; RECALL = the served asks whose reply landed under a marker (the chain is the replay) over all served asks; EFFICIENCY = the serves of the last day finished inside their latency class (a chat ask 30 s; work and events 180 s) over all serves; EXPERIENCE = the thumbs up over all thumbs given through the feedback door; COST = the spend a serving ask can be named for (the meter line wears the ask) over all spend. A measurement is UNKNOWN while nothing is there to measure — said, never a silent 1.0 — and an unknown turns no watch red. The kernel declares five watches at light (trust < 1.0 …) and ONE INTENTION, THE OPERATING STATE, beside Resiliency: the watch is the discriminator — the Operating State takes the measurements' reds, Resiliency every other red; its planner is asked under the red, its runner is the critic. THE GRADE BEAT makes the grader the consumer of live replies: every minute a few of the last hour's replies by a body (never a reviewer's own, never a grading ask) are handed to the grader under a GRADING marker beneath the reply's own ask (the hull's event edge), the evidence in the ask and the form in the answer — `grade: <A–F> — <one line>`; the grader writes its SIGNED verdict on the reply; a reply not graded in the form is said, never guessed. SPINE_GRADE_LIVE=0 turns the live grading off (it spends). THUMBS: click 👍 or 👎 under a reply — routine, recorded under your seat; it feeds Experience and the grader's evidence, never a body directly (raw feedback never reaches a body). THE IMPROVEMENT LOOP closes in the Workshop: an improvement marked on a body's reply reaches the critic (its event edge), which may call its PROPOSE tool once — a draft of that body's template, prompt, skill or graph lands UNDER THE BODY'S OWNER (the person who promoted it, else who registered its template, else the world's owner), marked “proposed by the critic from marker X”; the owner reads it in the Workshop (“load my bob draft in the workshop”), cuts it, and the Experiment judges it. SUMMON is generalized: “summon critic” (or any body whose template declares `summonable: true`; MITL by its own word; a helper never) joins this session's crew — its asks are an include's thoughts under the session's objective — and “dismiss critic” lets it go; both recorded. IMPORT runs a repo'd graph inside the hull: register a source of the repo form (“register the source bob-src …” through the shelf door: repo · commit · entry `module:attr`), then a graph with a node of kind `import` naming that source; the body fetches the commit once under its home (~/.orreth/imports) and runs the entry — a compiled LangGraph (`.invoke({"text"})` → `reply`) or a callable of the words — in a DEV universe only; a prod universe refuses in words. “show the measurements” (the Monitor pull) reads the five with their words.
